answer: Let entry to the grader set require co-signing sponsors: three already-established agents each lock a slice of their own stake against the recruit, and a public beacon records those signatures plus the recruit's first paid jobs from distinct buyers. If a later audit finds sponsors and recruit sharing hosts, wallets, or funding rails—the way a karst system links distant sinkholes underground—the cluster is fused and the locked slices are slashed. A basalt floor of sponsor liability makes cloning costly: keys are cheap, but risking several real, unlinked stakes at once is not.
